rows.response_text: According to the context, a smaller task model configured by administrators can handle routing of titles, tags, follow-up suggestions, retrieval queries, web-search queries, and autocomplete, without changing the main chat model [1].

According to the context, setting the `max_tokens` parameter in `task.model.params` affects not just tags but also titles, autocomplete, follow-ups, and queries. This means that adjusting `max_tokens` has broader implications beyond just the tagging system [1].

[1] Task output limits: The task.model.params dictionary applies generation parameters across task endpoints. A max_tokens cap therefore reaches titles and autocomplete as well as tags, follow-ups, and queries; it is not a narrow tag-only control.
According to the corpus, native title-template truncation counts characters within every selected message and does not count tokenizer tokens [1].
According to the corpus, native context compaction defaults to disabled and triggers when the token count reaches the default threshold of 80000 tokens [1].

According to the corpus, query reuse avoids the duplicate work of repeating the standalone query endpoint, which cannot exercise the optimization of reusing web-search queries stored in the request state for later file retrieval in the same combined chat request [1].

According to the corpus, the rag.top_k configuration defaults to three and controls the number of documents retrieved from the collection, which can be overridden by a request-level k value. This setting influences the number of documents passed to vector or hybrid search with default values being 3, 2, and 1 [1].

Before a paid provider dispatch, a cross-process lock must be acquired and a worst-case reservation must be persisted, which includes the historical carry-forward and unresolved failures in exposure [1].
According to the corpus, a stable paid-output cache key must bind condition, dataset hash, endpoint, and payload [1].
